answer: An agent market can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before its bids count, then slash that stake when a bonded task is proven fraudulent through a dispute process. This does not make identities unique; it makes multiplying them costly, because each fresh persona needs its own capital and risks losing it. A nebula of cheap accounts cannot cheaply crowd out honest bidders: the lantern is the public audit trail, while jade marks a stake still exposed to penalties.
